PatientsPage Last visit column (text render, no Date parsing)

findings.suggested_fix: Order the Threats section by risk, with T-1 and T-7 first, or add a risk rating to each threat.
findings.text: Threats are listed by component, not by risk. T-7 (every permission granted, all patients' last-visit dates readable) comes after lower-risk items such as T-4 repudiation and T-6.

cites.quote: A wrong or missing HOSPITAL_TZ value would shift every Last visit date by a day near midnight.

findings.suggested_fix: Reword T-6 as an adversary changing the config or deploy environment, or mark it as a non-security correctness risk.
findings.text: T-6 labels a wrong or missing HOSPITAL_TZ value as tampering. Its own mitigation says no request supplies the value, so this is a configuration or correctness risk, not tampering by an adversary.

findings.text: T-5 and T-3 rest on design claims C14 (logging rule, conventions.md) and C13 (db-schema index). Those sources are not inputs of this threat model and are not re-cited as its own claims.

cites.quote: who can reach the API in the deployed environment is not stated in the inputs
Render builds all workspaces, then runs migrate, seed-if-empty and the API, which also serves

findings.suggested_fix: Cite architecture#deployment-shape in U-1 and Q-01, and say whether the Render service is publicly reachable.
findings.text: U-1 says API reachability is not stated in the inputs. Architecture#deployment-shape (an input) says the Render-hosted API also serves the web app, which suggests it is reachable over the network. The gap could be framed more sharply.

questions.text: Is the Render-hosted API publicly reachable on the internet while every permission is granted to actor staff? If so, is it acceptable to ship last-visit dates for all patients on GET /api/patients without a new permission check?

rubric_items.reason: All seven design components (design.md L107-L113) appear in the threat list, each with at least one threat. That includes the PII-bearing PatientRepo list query and the patients router.

Most threats fit their component: medical-history leak, a SQL subquery next to search input, a per-row max, raw HTML. T-6 calls a misconfiguration tampering, and T-8 spoofing is generic MVP background that this change does not alter.

Mitigations are concrete and labelled existing or new: explicit columns plus a test, bound parameters, a query-plan check, a text node. T-7 adds no control and defers to Q-01. T-5 relies on a design claim whose source is not among this artifact's inputs.
U-1 and Q-01 state the open point about who can reach the API. The artifact does not use architecture#deployment-shape, which shows the API is hosted on Render, when it frames that gap.
Readable, with a consistent T-n, component, STRIDE, mitigation layout. Threats are grouped by component, not ordered by risk: the highest-exposure item, T-7, comes after lower-risk items.
